segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I pulled up the order form in the CRM. We have you at 42 seats today, renewing on October 1, and you had asked about moving to 55 seats for the operations team. Is that still the right count?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yes, 55 is right. We had 52 confirmed and I want 3 extra for new hires in November. I just need the invoice to show one annual line item if possible.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, we can do that. The pricing sheet has the 55-seat tier at $84 per seat per month, billed annually, so the subscription total is $55,440. Implementation support is already complete, so there is no services line this time.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And payment terms are still net 30? Our finance team will ask because last year the invoice said due on receipt and it caused a little back and forth.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Good catch. I’ll make sure the billing tool has net 30 on the invoice. Contract start October 1, end September 30 next year, total $55,440, net 30. No auto-renew language changes from last year.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. Can you send the order form today? Our VP can sign tomorrow if it’s clean.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I can send it by 3 pm Central. I’ll route it through deal desk first because the seat increase is over 25 percent, but that’s usually a same-day approval.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Also, we need access for the 13 new users on October 2, not October 1. We’re doing a short internal training that morning.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. I’ll note October 2 as the enablement date for the new seats. Existing 42 users continue without interruption on October 1.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send it over and I’ll watch for it.
